title: Route-aware prefilter with shadow-decommit to eliminate hot-path trace allocations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Recent deployment of the unified tracing SDK increased p99 tail latency in the HTTP ingress path by ~2-3ms for high-QPS routes. Root cause analysis shows allocation churn and mutex contention from the full span construction path on the hot path (when most requests are not going to be sampled).

Goal: Reduce hot-path CPU and allocation overhead when tracing is disabled or unlikely to sample while preserving tail-based and adaptive sampling signals for post-hoc analysis. Target: reduce additional CPU cycles per request by >= 60% and allocations by >= 70% for non-sampled requests on top-100 routes.

Proposal: Implement a route-aware prefilter that makes a low-cost sampling decision before any span object allocation, combined with a "shadow-decommit" mechanism: if the prefilter decides to "not sample", record a tiny shadow datum (route id + hashed decision + trace id prefix) in a lock-free ring buffer that is flushed periodically to a background worker. If tail-sampling later decides the request should be surfaced, the background worker will reconstruct minimal context and trigger a lightweight instrumentation job that enriches samples only for the subset flagged via shadow-decommit.

Key components:
- Ingress prefilter: deterministic, per-route probabilistic table updated from control plane. Uses a 32-bit hash of (route, user-agent, short trace-id) and a per-route sampling rate. No heap allocation; operates on stack and inline bit-ops.
- Shadow decommit buffer: per-thread fixed-size ring buffer (configurable 8k entries) that stores 12-byte records (route-id idx, timestamp delta, 24-bit trace prefix). Implemented with atomic head/tail indices to avoid locks.
- Background reconstructor: async worker co-located on non-hot cores that consumes buffers, batches writes to durable telemetry store (compressed format) and triggers a low-priority enrichment pass if tail-sampling heuristics match.
- Control plane hooks: policy API to update per-route rates, enable/disable shadow capture, and mark routes eligible for decommit enrichment.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Pros: eliminates most allocations and mutex acquisitions on the hot path; preserves ability to recover traces for tail-sampling without expensive full-span capture for every request.
- Cons: shadow-decommit is best-effort; if background worker crashes, some recoverability is lost. Adds complexity to control plane syncing. There is additional latency in reconstructing traces for late sampling decisions (acceptable for diagnostics).

Acceptance criteria:
- Hot-path per-request allocations reduced by >= 70% for non-sampled requests on top-100 routes (benchmarked with our microbench harness).
- P99 latency regression < 0.5 ms compared to baseline without tracing enabled for the same routes.
- End-to-end tail-sample recovery rate >= 95% for injected fault traces in stress tests.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Spike: implemented C micro-bench for null-prefilter vs full-span; null-prefilter path shows 12 allocations->0 and ~2.5x CPU reduction. Prototype located in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/tree/feat/prefilter-spike (WIP).

2026-03-04 - Design review with Observability: approved route-indexing approach, asked for explicit backstop to avoid buffer overrun (circuit-breaker in background worker). Assigned Diego for implementation and Eva for stress testing.
2026-03-06 - Decision: use per-thread ring buffer to avoid cross-thread contention; buffer size default 8192 entries, configurable via ENV. Added measurement hooks for head/tail counters.
2026-03-08 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1427 - prefilter + ring buffer skeleton. CI failing on race in buffer flush; fixing atomic ordering in consumer.
2026-03-10 - Perf results from integration test: allocations down 68% on top-20 routes, median latency unchanged, p99 reduced by 1.8ms on one noisy route. Need soak for 48h before rollout.

2026-03-12 - Security review note: shadow buffer contains trace-id prefix; storing prefixes considered low-risk but team requested KMS policy for telemetry export endpoints. Filed dependency ENG-90711 for export RBAC.
